- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.25) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–4% to match true mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.25–0.67); use 3–5 day moving average of recent 18-day history to anchor forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift timing.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overestimating continuation.
